output.summary: A deciduous tree native across much of Europe and northern Anatolia, it also has isolated populations from northwestern Africa to northwestern Iran. Its fruit is edible but astringent and gritty straight from the tree; after overripening it sweetens, and it is also made into drinks, jam, juice and brandy.
output.edibilityNote: Fruit is edible; it sweetens after overripening and is used for cider-like drinks, jam, juice and brandy. Ancient Greeks also pickled it.
